architectural_insight: The architecture demonstrates clean separation of concerns with specialized roles (measurement, persistence, presentation), but ModularDashboard's central orchestration creates a dependency bottleneck that violates the Single Responsibility Principle. The persistence layer's built-in migration logic indicates mature handling of schema evolution, though the tight coupling between grid measurement and layout engine suggests missing abstraction layers for coordinate system contracts.
coupling_risks: ModularDashboard exhibits God Component anti-pattern with high fan-in (imports 5/6 members), creating a single point of failure and preventing independent component evolution
Implicit grid unit contract between AutoHeightPanel and DashboardGrid lacks explicit shared interface/types for height-to-grid conversion logic
useLayoutPersistence tightly coupled to specific panel data schema, requiring complex migration logic when structure changes
Barrel file (index.ts) couples external consumers to internal implementation details, hindering refactoring without breaking changes
Circular data flow risk: AutoHeightPanel measurements trigger layout updates which may cause re-measurement loops if not debounced properly
data_flow: useLayoutPersistence hydrates initial layout state from localStorage into ModularDashboard, which acts as the central orchestrator. ModularDashboard passes responsive grid configuration to DashboardGrid, which manages the react-grid-layout engine. DashboardGrid renders PanelChrome containers for each panel, which wrap AutoHeightPanel to measure content height and convert pixel measurements to grid units for dynamic resizing. architectural_insight: This group exhibits a classic React monolithic root anti-pattern where App.tsx serves as a dense composition root with excessive orchestration responsibilities. The SettingsDrawer->AdvancedSettingsPanel chain suggests deep nesting that could benefit from compound component patterns or context providers to reduce prop drilling. Consider extracting the health-check orchestration and settings management into custom hooks or state machines to decouple the startup sequence from the presentation layer
blast_radius: src/codrag/dashboard/src/App.tsx (affected by changes to any child component signature)
src/codrag/dashboard/src/components/UpdateBanner.tsx (affected by App.tsx layout or lifecycle changes)
coupling_risks: App.tsx is a 'God Component' with direct concrete imports to 5 specific components, creating rigid coupling to implementation details rather than abstractions
SettingsDrawer has tight concrete dependency on AdvancedSettingsPanel, preventing mock substitution or alternative panel implementations
StartupScreen is likely tightly coupled to App's specific connection state management interface (props/callbacks)
Risk of prop drilling from App through SettingsDrawer to AdvancedSettingsPanel for global settings state
App.tsx mixes multiple orthogonal concerns (health monitoring, auto-updates, theming, settings persistence) in a single orchestration layer

During initialization, StartupScreen polls the backend /health endpoint and reports status upward to App.tsx. App.tsx conditionally renders the main dashboard or startup screen based on health state.
